The paper presents the first active acoustic illusion technique using arrays of monopole control sources and error sensors.
The technique enables illusions such as changing the apparent size or location of an object, or replacing its scattered field with that of a different incident field.
The method does not require changes to the control configuration to achieve different types of illusions.
Two control configurations are used: circumferential arrays for global illusions and line arrays for forward-scatter illusions.
The global illusion configuration uses 20 control sources and 40 error sensors arranged circumferentially around the cylinder.
The forward-scatter illusion configuration uses 200 control sources and 400 error sensors equally distributed along the line arrays from -60a to 60a.
Experiments are conducted at 200 Hz.
The radius of the rigid cylinder used in the simulations is 0.6 meters.
The fluid medium is air with a density of 1.225 kg/m³ and a speed of sound of 343 m/s.
The cost function for sound cancellation is J = e^H e, where e is the total acoustic field at the error sensors.
The optimal control source strength for sound cancellation is q = -[Z^H Z]^-1 Z^H p.
When the perimeter of the illusion object is enclosed within the control source perimeter, the illusion field takes effect beyond the control source perimeter.
When the perimeter of the illusion object exceeds the control source perimeter, the illusion takes effect from the illusion object perimeter, reducing the size of the acoustic illusion domain.
The technique can work for a rigid body of arbitrary shape by implementing a numerical solution to obtain the primary and secondary acoustic responses.
Potential applications include masking unwanted sound and misrepresenting information about a target for stealth purposes.
The method is demonstrated for both global and forward-scatter illusions.
The technique depends on prior knowledge of the incident field and the primary acoustic field arising from scattering of an incident field by a rigid body.
The analytical simulations were conducted within MATLAB.
Analytical results were numerically validated using COMSOL Multiphysics 5.4.
The fluid medium is considered inviscid and free of losses for the simulations.
The system parameters include a 2D rigid cylinder of radius 0.6 m in air.
The technique can generate multiple illusions simultaneously with a fixed control configuration.
The size of the domain of the illusional field is strongly dependent on the number and placement of the control sources and error sensors.
It is not possible to actively generate an illusional field in the back-scatter region using the line array configuration due to the requirement to cancel the primary incident field.
